data.gender_notes: Ljerka is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Slavic word for 'light', Ljerka is a name evoking beauty and radiance. It may also be associated with the saint Ljeria, a martyr venerated in the Eastern Orthodox Church. The name Ljerka carries the meaning “Light, Beautiful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ljerka usually hope their child will grow to embody light, beautiful and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ljerka total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: According to local legend, Ljerka of Dubrovnik was a 16th century woman known for her exceptional beauty and virtuous character. She was said to have been the inspiration for the poem 'Lijepa Štole' (Beautiful Chest) by Marin Držić. The poem celebrated Ljerka's beauty while also encouraging religious devotion.

Another legend tells the story of Ljerka of Sinj, a 19th century woman who lived in the town of Sinj, Croatia. She was a shepherdess who was brutally murdered by Ottoman invaders. According to the legend, her body was found with a miraculous image of the Virgin Mary on her chest, which is now venerated as a sacred relic.
